g.text: §1 INTRODUCTION
The last mile of research is a separate layer, prepared in the days after
acceptance, and three gaps remain open
Poster, talk video, and blog piece each need figure selection, layout, narration, or audience-appropriate writing (§1)
The dissemination layer covers the poster you stand next to at a conference session, the talk video on the venue's virtual track or the lab's channel, and
the blog piece shared through social media. Authors prepare all three in the days right after acceptance, at exactly the moment they have the least time
to spare; labs, courses, and multilingual organizations reuse the same layer.
Paper-to-poster, paper-to-video, and paper-to-blog systems, plus the multi-artifact suites PaperX and OmniPresent, shift the question from whether

text.tspan: several formats can be generated to whether the artifacts remain native-editable and navigable.

g.text: G1
Shared grounding
Combining artifact-specific systems repeats
figure, caption, and metadata extraction, and
leaves cross-artifact references for the user to
reconcile.
G2
Native editability
A multi-format suite does not by itself give
native-editable source files for every artifact in
the author's PowerPoint and Word workflow.
G3
Experience-level convergence
Parallel or consistently rendered outputs do not
bind poster regions, video segments, and blog
passages into one interactive surface for
revision and reuse.
WHO ELSE THE LAST MILE SERVES (§1)
The accepted-paper author
the poster, talk video, and blog piece prepared in the days after
acceptance, right after the camera-ready
An industrial research lab
public-facing communications for every accepted paper,
polished by a communications team
A course or multilingual organization
a graduate course's paper-of-the-week briefing pack;
cross-region outreach in more than one language
Source: arXiv:2607.04438 v2 (19 Jul 2026)
